overviewParagraphs: Alpine Golf Resort Chiang Mai is widely regarded as one of the most scenic golf experiences in all of Thailand. Ron Garl's design sits in a spectacular mountain valley surrounded by the ranges of Northern Thailand, offering elevation changes, mountain vistas, and a cool highland climate that makes playing here feel closer to New Zealand than Southeast Asia.

The layout uses the natural valley terrain to create a flowing course where every hole feels organically routed — there are no artificial mounds or manufactured features, just the honest golf that emerges when a skilled architect works with strong natural material. The result is a course of beauty and genuine strategic challenge.

Chiang Mai is an outstanding golf destination for discerning travellers who want to combine great golf with cultural immersion in Thailand's most charming city. AGS regularly builds week-long Chiang Mai itineraries pairing multiple rounds with temple visits, night markets, and elephant sanctuary experiences.

curatorBriefHtml: Alpine Golf Resort Chiang Mai (opened 2008 by Ron Garl in the San Kamphaeng valley) is Northern Thailand’s most refined mountain parkland resort — sitting 30 minutes east of Chiang Mai’s Old City amidst rice fields and towering teak forests. Playing 6,904 yards from the Blue Tees (Par 72), the 27-hole facility delivers rolling mounding, pristine conditioning, and strategic creek crossings framed by cool northern hill views.

Unlike Bangkok’s flat, humid layouts, Chiang Mai sits in a refreshing northern valley where November through February mornings start crisp around 16–20°C. Alpine Chiang Mai’s generous resort fairways make it welcoming for mid-handicappers while deep greenside bunkers and slick sloping greens demand deft short-game touch.
On our Lanna Heritage Golf Trail, AGS pairs Alpine Chiang Mai with Chiang Mai Highlands and Mae Jo from boutique Lanna bases such as Tamarind Village or Four Seasons Chiang Mai.

scorecard.verdict: Nestled in the San Kamphaeng valley surrounded by misty mountain ranges. Host of multiple Asian Tour events, Alpine Chiang Mai tests ball-striking with dramatic lake carries and sweeping valley fairways.

faqs.q: How far is Alpine Golf Resort Chiang Mai from Chiang Mai city?
faqs.a: Allow 30 to 40 minutes east of central Chiang Mai and Chiang Mai International Airport (CNX) by private touring vehicle.

faqs.q: How does Alpine Chiang Mai compare to Chiang Mai Highlands?
faqs.a: Both are Northern Thailand’s premier tracks. Alpine Chiang Mai plays as a polished, resort-style valley parkland layout with on-site stay-and-play convenience, whereas Chiang Mai Highlands climbs higher into dramatic mountain foothills with bolder elevation swings.

faqs.q: When is the best season to golf in Chiang Mai?
faqs.a: November through February is Northern Thailand’s peak cool, dry season (16–28°C). Note that March–April can see regional agricultural haze, so AGS prioritizes November–February and June–October green-season mornings.

faqs.q: Can groups stay directly on-site at Alpine Golf Resort Chiang Mai?
faqs.a: Yes, though most AGS guests prefer staying in central Chiang Mai or Mae Rim to enjoy Chiang Mai’s acclaimed dining and night markets after morning golf.
